strengths: Novel contribution: Per-instance noise scheduling guided by image power spectrum is creative and well-motivated
Solid theoretical foundation: Clear analysis connecting spectral properties to noise levels with formal bounds on efficacy
Comprehensive experimental design: Evaluation across multiple resolutions and model sizes with good ablations
Clear presentation: Well-written with effective visualizations and clearly specified algorithms
Practical improvements in low-step regime: Demonstrates benefits for fast generation scenarios
Proper mathematical treatment: Variance-preserving assumptions and closed-form schedule solutions provided
weaknesses: Modest empirical improvements: Typically <1 FID gain over SiD2; gains disappear at higher step counts
Severely limited evaluation scope: Only ImageNet evaluated; no other domains or tasks assessed
Not applicable to latent diffusion: Restricts to pixel-space single-stage diffusion, increasingly obsolete compared to dominant latent approaches
Computational overhead unaddressed: RAPSD computation per training image cost not quantified or discussed
Hyperparameter sensitivity: Table 5 shows >10% FID variation with different κ values; selection appears ad-hoc
Reproducibility concerns: RAPSD sampling details vague, hyperparameter selection unclear, no code availability mentioned
Limited technical novelty: Core contribution is spectrum fitting and noise scaling; standard components throughout
Loose theoretical bounds: Analysis in Section 4.2 proves existence but lacks practical insight
Power-law assumption robustness unclear: Empirical assumption (Eq. 8) and violation consequences not discussed
Incomplete explanation: Doesn't explain why improvements vanish at higher step counts or when method is preferred

strengths: Novel and well-motivated approach using image spectral properties to guide per-instance noise schedules, with elegant theoretical justification through rigorous RAPSD analysis

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three resolutions (128², 256², 512²) with multiple metrics, showing consistent improvements especially in the practically-important low-step regime (32-64 steps: 5-15% FID improvements)
Thorough ablation studies systematically validating design choices including schedule variants, FiLM conditioning, and guidance intervals, strengthening the contribution
Solid mathematical framework with clear derivations from spectral properties to noise level bounds and closed-form schedules, with proper variance-preserving assumptions
Excellent presentation and clarity with effective visualizations (Figures 1-3) that clearly convey the method's concept and benefits; detailed implementation details enable reproducibility
Significant practical value: achieving better generation quality with fewer denoising steps directly addresses key efficiency concerns in diffusion model deployment
weaknesses: Conceptual novelty is somewhat incremental: while the application is clever, the core insight that different frequencies warrant different noise treatment follows fairly naturally from natural image statistics
Improvements diminish substantially at higher step counts: at optimal NFE (256 steps for 256²), FID improvement is modest (~7%), limiting applicability for high-quality generation scenarios

Experimental scope is limited to ImageNet class-conditional generation only; lacks evaluation on other datasets, domains, unconditional generation, and text-to-image applications where diffusion models are widely deployed
Theoretical justification relies partially on empirical observations: the maximum noise derivation uses the heuristic condition Ψ_zₑ(q) ≫ 1 without rigorous formal justification of its validity
Computational overhead not quantified: DFT computation for each training image during RAPSD estimation is not measured or discussed; potential impact on training time unclear
Method introduces hyperparameters (κ_min, κ_max, κ_p) requiring resolution-specific tuning (Table 5), reducing generality; systematic sensitivity analysis could be more thorough
Missing important ablations: no direct comparison between per-instance adaptation vs. simpler baseline using fixed global schedule derived from training set median RAPSD
Incomplete failure mode analysis: no discussion of performance on images with atypical spectral properties, synthetic/out-of-distribution images, or other potential edge cases

strengths: Novel per-instance noise scheduling idea grounded in image spectral properties, with clear intuitive motivation (Figure 1)
Solid mathematical framework deriving expected RAPSD after noise addition and bounds on effective noise levels
Comprehensive experiments across multiple resolutions and datasets with fair comparisons against SiD2 baseline
Practical advantages including 3× speedup at optimal steps and no per-resolution hyperparameter tuning
Thorough ablation studies isolating individual contributions and investigating FID degradation at high NFE
Well-executed presentation with clear algorithms, good visualizations, and complete implementation details
weaknesses: Theoretical bounds (κ_min, κ_max) lack rigorous justification; choice of κ_max=100, κ_min=0.01 appears ad-hoc
Mixed schedule design (λ_M = 0.5(λ_F + λ_P)) acknowledged as heuristic, contradicting 'principled' framing; no justification for averaging weights
Power law approximation Ψ̃(k)=βk^α uses only 2 parameters without validating approximation error or sensitivity analysis
Modest empirical improvements in standard regimes (FID gains of 0.05-0.26) with most benefits concentrated in low-step regime
FID degradation at high NFE suggests tight schedules have fundamental limitations; degradation appears earlier than baseline, requiring γ=0.5 adjustment
Poor generalization across domains: text-to-image oracle (6.55 FID) significantly outperforms sampler (7.18 FID), indicating RAPSD sampler doesn't generalize
Significant architectural modifications beyond noise scheduling (min/max logSNR conditioning, t-based guidance intervals) make it difficult to isolate the pure contribution
Results lag substantially behind SOTA (LDMs reach 1.13 FID; method reaches 1.32-1.45), limiting practical impact in field dominated by latent diffusion
Hyperparameter choices (C=5/10 for GMM components, κ values) lack principled justification or sensitivity analysis
Scope limited to single-stage pixel diffusion, which is increasingly sidelined by LDMs and distilled models
